title: 第396章 急转直下第385章 相似的花
slug: 长生从守书阁的太监开始
lines: 第396章急转直下
又是五年过去。
时光的长河奔腾不息，冲刷着人间的繁华与疮痍。
曾经被被世人交口称赞的庆顺盛世，此刻回想起来，竟恍如隔世幻梦，又似一朵在夜空中极致绽放后迅速湮灭的烟花，绚烂，却短暂得令人心悸。
五年前，大乾王朝似乎还处在国力蒸蒸日上的巅峰。
皇帝励精图治，朝堂虽暗流涌动但大体稳定，边境无大战事，国内虽偶有小灾，但总体风调雨顺，仓廪渐丰，市井繁华。
谁能想到，盛世的根基竟如此脆弱？
仿佛一夜之间，天地便翻了脸。
先是北方数道接连三年大旱，赤地千里，河湖见底，庄稼颗粒无收，饿殍遍野。
紧接着，南方诸省又遭遇百年不遇的连绵暴雨，江河溃决，洪水滔天，吞噬田园屋舍，瘟疫随之肆虐。
朝廷初时还竭力调拨钱粮赈济，派遣重臣巡视灾区，整饬河工。
然而，天灾仿佛没有尽头，这里旱情未解，那里洪峰又至；这边瘟疫刚有控制之势，那边地动山摇屋舍成墟。
国库以惊人的速度空虚，地方官吏贪墨赈灾钱粮、中饱私囊的丑闻却不断爆出。
流民如潮水般从受灾地区涌出，向着想象中的富庶之地迁徙，沿途乞讨、抢掠，与当地居民冲突不断，社会秩序开始崩坏。
与此同时，各地蛰伏已久、或因天灾人祸而活不下去的豪强、匪类、乃至对朝廷心怀怨望的前朝遗族、地方大姓，纷纷趁机揭竿而起。
有的打着替天行道的旗号，有的则直接称王称帝，割据一方。
起初只是星星之火，在官府看来不过是疥癣之疾，然而朝廷大军疲于奔命四处救火，却因粮饷不济、将领无能、士气低落而屡战屡败，反而让叛军坐大。
烽火迅速蔓延，从边陲到腹地，从山林到平原，大乾江山，四处冒烟。
而最令朝廷头疼、也最让有识之士脊背发寒的，是白莲教的死灰复燃，且其势之猛，远超以往。
在连续的天灾和战乱中，无数百姓家园破碎，亲人离散，朝不保夕，对未来充满绝望。
白莲教那套教义，恰如黑暗中的鬼火，对绝望的民众产生了致命的吸引力。
大量流民、溃兵、失地农民涌入教中，白莲教迅速膨胀，不再满足于地下传播，开始公然攻占州县，建立政教合一的割据势力。
他们手段酷烈，对不信教者乃至普通教众都拥有生杀予夺之权，所过之处，往往玉石俱焚，比寻常叛军更为可怕。
面对这糜烂的局势，紫禁城中的庆顺帝，心路历程却令人扼腕。
起初，他或许还存有重振朝纲、平定天下的雄心，日夜操劳，调兵遣将，甚至一度御驾亲征。
然而，坏消息如同雪片般飞来，国库空空如也，朝中党争却愈演愈烈，前方将帅或跋扈不听调遣，或庸懦不堪一战。
更可怕的是，不知从何时起，朝野内外开始流传一种声音，将这天灾人祸、烽烟四起的乱象，归咎于陛下失德，触怒上天，故而降下灾劫。
这种流言起初隐秘，后来竟逐渐公开化，连一些清流言官也开始或明或暗地上书，言辞间虽不敢直指天子，但修德省身、回应天谴之意昭然若揭。

Chapter 396 A sudden turn of events
Another five years have passed.
The long river of time is endless, washing away the prosperity and devastation of the world.
The prosperous age of Qingshun, which was once praised by the world, now looks back like a dream from another life, or like a firework that blooms in the night sky and then quickly annihilates. It is gorgeous, but so short-lived that it is heart-stopping.
Five years ago, the Daqian Dynasty seemed to be at the peak of its national power.
The emperor worked hard to govern, and although there were undercurrents in the court, it was generally stable. There were no wars on the border. Although there were occasional minor disasters in the country, the overall situation was smooth, the warehouses were increasingly abundant, and the markets were prosperous.
Who would have thought that the foundation of the prosperous age could be so fragile?
As if overnight, the world turned upside down.
First, there was severe drought for three consecutive years in the north. Thousands of miles of bare land, rivers and lakes bottomed out, no crops were harvested, and people died of hunger all over the land.
Immediately afterwards, the southern provinces suffered from continuous heavy rains that had not been seen in a century. Rivers burst and floods devoured rural houses, and the plague raging subsequently.
At the beginning, the imperial court tried its best to allocate money and food for relief, and sent important ministers to inspect the disaster areas and rectify the river works.
However, there seems to be no end to the natural disasters. The drought here is not resolved, and the flood peak is coming there again; here the plague has just been under control, and there the earth is shaking and the mountains are shaking the houses into ruins.
The national treasury is emptying at an alarming rate, and scandals continue to surface about local officials embezzling disaster relief money and lining their own pockets.
Refugees poured out of the disaster-stricken areas like a tide, migrating toward imaginary wealthy lands, begging and looting along the way, and constantly clashed with local residents, and social order began to collapse.
At the same time, powerful men and bandits in various places who had been dormant for a long time, or who were unable to survive due to natural disasters or man-made disasters, and even the survivors of the previous dynasty and local surnames who were resentful of the imperial court, took the opportunity to rise up.
Some used the banner of upholding justice for heaven, while others directly proclaimed themselves kings and emperors, separatist power.
At first, it was just a spark, and in the eyes of the government, it was just a scabies disease. However, the imperial army was exhausted in running around to put out the fire. However, due to insufficient food and pay, incompetent generals, and low morale, they suffered repeated defeats, which only allowed the rebels to gain strength.
The beacon fire spread rapidly, from the border to the hinterland, from the mountains and forests to the plains, and smoke was rising everywhere.
What caused the most headache for the court and sent chills down the spines of knowledgeable people was the resurgence of the White Lotus Sect, which was far more powerful than before.
In the continuous natural disasters and wars, countless people's homes have been shattered, their relatives separated, their lives are precarious, and they are full of despair about the future.
The teachings of the White Lotus Sect are like a will-o'-the-wisp in the darkness, exerting a fatal attraction on the desperate people.
A large number of refugees, defeated soldiers, and landless farmers poured into the religion. The White Lotus Sect expanded rapidly. No longer content with spreading underground, it began to openly occupy prefectures and counties, establishing a separatist force that integrated politics and religion.
Their methods are ruthless, and they have the power of life and death against unbelievers and even ordinary believers. Wherever they go, everyone is often destroyed, making them more terrifying than ordinary rebels.
Faced with this corrupt situation, Emperor Qingshun's mental journey in the Forbidden City was disappointing.
At first, he may have had the ambition to revitalize the imperial court and pacify the world. He worked day and night, dispatched troops and generals, and even once led a personal expedition.
However, bad news is coming like snow flakes, the treasury is empty, the party dispute between North Korea and China is intensifying, and the generals at the front are either domineering and unwilling to listen to orders, or they are cowardly and unable to fight.
What's even more frightening is that, from unknown time on, a voice began to spread both inside and outside the court, blaming the natural and man-made disasters and the chaos of wars on His Majesty's lack of morality and angering God, thus bringing down the disaster.
This kind of rumor was secretive at first, but later it gradually became public. Even some Qing gossip officials began to write openly or covertly. Although they did not dare to point directly at the emperor, their intention to practice morality and self-reflection and respond to divine punishment was clear.
